$comment: FROZEN. These are conformance vectors for the .chiro.json canonicalisation and validation rules. Once published they must never change: other implementations check themselves against them. If a value here is wrong, publish a corrected vector set under a new spec_version rather than editing these in place. The file is deliberately pure ASCII (\uXXXX escapes) so that the NFC/NFD cases are unambiguous about which codepoints they mean. 'canonical' is the exact string that gets UTF-8 encoded and hashed, carried literally so that a mismatching implementation can diff the STRING rather than stare at two digests. Any body_hash here can be re-derived with no chirograph code at all: printf '%s' "<canonical>" | md5sum. 'dvc_dir' / 'dvc_dir_hash' are the DERIVED DVC .dir interop form (spec §0), which uses DIFFERENT serialisation (default separators, ensure_ascii=True, no size field) and therefore a different hash — see docs/decisions.md D-01.

canonicalisation.name: empty
canonicalisation.why: A manifest may legitimately describe zero files. The canonical form of an empty array is '[]' — two bytes, not the empty string.

canonicalisation.name: single-minimal
canonicalisation.why: The smallest real case: one entry with only the three required fields. Keys come out alphabetically (md5, relpath, size), not in declaration order.

canonicalisation.name: unsorted-input
canonicalisation.why: Canonicalisation sorts; the on-disk order of the input must not affect the hash. Same expected output as 'sorted-input'.

canonicalisation.name: sorted-input
canonicalisation.why: The same entries already in order. Must hash identically to 'unsorted-input'.

canonicalisation.name: key-order-scrambled
canonicalisation.why: Keys given in a deliberately odd order. sort_keys=True must make this identical to 'single-minimal'.

canonicalisation.name: sort-hyphen-before-slash
canonicalisation.why: THE sort trap. The sort key is the joined POSIX path as a plain string, not a tuple of components. '-' is U+002D and '/' is U+002F, so 'a-b/x' sorts BEFORE 'a/b'. An implementation that splits into components first, or that sorts by (dirname, basename), gets the opposite order and a different hash.

canonicalisation.name: sort-case-sensitive
canonicalisation.why: Sorting is by codepoint, not case-folded or locale-aware. All ASCII uppercase precedes all ASCII lowercase, so 'B.txt' sorts before 'a.txt'. A locale-aware sort (or Python's `sorted(key=str.lower)`) reverses this.

canonicalisation.name: nfd-input-normalised
canonicalisation.why: Input carries a decomposed e-acute (e + U+0301, as macOS produces). The canonical form carries the composed U+00E9. An implementation that skips NFC normalisation produces a manifest that a Linux-built one cannot match.

canonicalisation.name: nfc-then-sort-ordering-trap
canonicalisation.why: THE order-of-operations trap. Normalise BEFORE sorting. In NFD, 'cafe\u0301' sorts before 'caff' (compare 'e' U+0065 with 'f' U+0066). After NFC it is 'caf\u00e9', which sorts AFTER 'caff' (U+00E9 > U+0066). Sort-then-normalise yields the reverse order and a different hash.

canonicalisation.name: non-ascii-literal-in-canonical
canonicalisation.why: ensure_ascii=False: non-ASCII codepoints appear as literal UTF-8 in the canonical bytes, NOT as \uXXXX escapes. Contrast the dvc_dir field of this same case, which does escape them — that difference is precisely why body_hash is not a DVC .dir hash.

canonicalisation.name: astral-plane-codepoint
canonicalisation.why: A codepoint above U+FFFF (U+1F9EC DNA DOUBLE HELIX), which is one 4-byte UTF-8 sequence but a surrogate PAIR in UTF-16. Implementations that sort or length-check in UTF-16 code units diverge here.

canonicalisation.name: source-path-relocation
canonicalisation.why: Spec §8.1: a flat GEO deposit reorganised into a per-sample tree. source_path is included in the canonical form and sorts after 'size' alphabetically.

canonicalisation.name: redundant-source-path
canonicalisation.why: A source_path identical to its relpath. Canonicalisation does NOT drop it, so this hashes DIFFERENTLY from 'terse-no-source-path' below even though the two describe the same fetch. Writers omit redundant source_path; canonicalisers must not remove it, or two implementations disagree about which normalisations to apply. See docs/decisions.md D-06.

canonicalisation.name: terse-no-source-path
canonicalisation.why: The same fetch expressed tersely. Deliberately paired with 'redundant-source-path' to pin that the two body_hash values differ.

canonicalisation.name: extension-fields
canonicalisation.why: All DVC-compat and supplementary fields present at once, to pin their key ordering (etag, isexec, md5, relpath, size, source_path, version_id) and that booleans serialise as bare true/false.

canonicalisation.name: file-version-in-body
canonicalisation.why: (1.1) A file_version entry field. It is an ordinary scalar entry field, so it enters canonicalisation and IS covered by body_hash, sorting between 'etag' and 'isexec'. Paired with 'terse-no-source-path' (the same entry without it) to pin that adding the 1.1 field changes body_hash — i.e. it really enters the body.

canonicalisation.name: large-size-beyond-double
canonicalisation.why: 2**53 + 1 = 9007199254740993 bytes (~9 PB). Exactly representable as a JSON integer but NOT as an IEEE-754 double: a parser that routes integers through a float writes 9007199254740992 and gets a different hash. Real genomics archives are not yet this big, but a JSON parser choosing floats is a live hazard in several languages.

canonicalisation.name: zero-size
canonicalisation.why: A zero-byte file. size serialises as bare 0, and the md5 is the md5 of the empty string.

canonicalisation.name: duplicate-md5-two-paths
canonicalisation.why: Identical content at two paths — legal, and mirrors DVC's content-addressed dedup (one cache object, two paths). Not a duplicate entry: relpath is what must be unique.

canonicalisation.name: path-with-url-unsafe-characters
canonicalisation.why: Spaces, '#', '%', '?' and '+' in paths. These are legal filenames and must pass through canonicalisation untouched — percent-encoding belongs to URL resolution, not to the manifest.

canonicalisation.name: deep-nesting
canonicalisation.why: A long path, to pin that nothing collapses or normalises interior components.

canonicalisation.name: sha256-algorithm
canonicalisation.why: hash_algorithm sha256. The wire key stays 'md5' (spec §3.2 defines it as 'hash of the file's bytes, per hash_algorithm'); only the digest length and the algorithm used for body_hash change.

canonicalisation.name: many-entries-adversarial-order
canonicalisation.why: 200 entries interleaving upper- and lower-case stems, supplied in reverse. Catches sort instability and any accidental dependence on input order.

container_canonicalisation.name: container-body
container_canonicalisation.why: (2.0) A ZIP container plus one member carrying crc32. body_hash is over the two-key {containers, files} document (container-model §4): sort_keys fixes the top-level order as 'containers' then 'files', each array pre-sorted by its own key, container fields sorted alphabetically (format, md5, size, source_root).

container_canonicalisation.name: container-multi-sorted
container_canonicalisation.why: (2.0) Two containers given out of order, to pin that containers sort by source_root just as files sort by relpath.

path_safety.$comment: Paths that must be accepted and rejected on READ as well as write (spec §3.2). Rejection is a security boundary: a consumer materialises relpath to disk, and observed-download manifests describe other people's deposits.

accept.why: a leading dot is a normal filename, not a traversal
TWO leading dots followed by more characters is a filename, not '..'
dots in the middle of a component
hyphen sorts before slash but is perfectly legal
non-ASCII (decomposed; accepted, then normalised to NFC)
a colon is legal on POSIX away from position 1; only a leading DRIVE prefix like 'C:' is rejected

reject.why: absolute POSIX path - would escape the import target
empty interior component; ambiguous on materialisation
trailing separator; this names a directory, not a file
interior traversal - the classic Zip-Slip shape
backslash: a separator on one platform and a filename character on another
newline; a control character, and it breaks every line-oriented tool

manifests.$comment: Whole-document cases. 'valid' must load; each entry in 'invalid' must be refused with the named error class.

valid.name: observed-download-terse
valid.why: Spec §8.2: layout preserved, so no source_path and the body is DVC-.dir-shaped.

valid.name: minor-1-staleness-fields
valid.why: (1.1) The optional staleness fields (spec §8): concept and record_version in the header, file_version per entry. Must load, and schema_version is 1.1 because 1.1 fields are present.

valid.name: minor-2-container
valid.why: (2.0) A container block plus a ZIP member with crc32. Must load; body_hash is over the two-key {containers, files} document.

invalid.name: wrong-schema-token
invalid.why: The internal schema field is the fallback identifier; a reader must key on it.

invalid.name: future-major-version
invalid.why: A MAJOR version beyond what the reader implements (major 2) means it cannot be trusted to interpret the document. (2.0 is now a supported major — the container block — so the too-new major is 3.)

invalid.name: etag-algorithm
invalid.why: hash_algorithm 'etag' is reserved but rejected in v1 (docs/decisions.md D-04).

invalid.name: body-hash-mismatch
invalid.why: The load-bearing check: a files array that does not match its body_hash.

invalid.name: nfiles-disagrees
invalid.why: Cheap sanity check from spec §9 step 4.

invalid.name: size-disagrees
invalid.why: Cheap sanity check from spec §9 step 4.

invalid.name: traversal-relpath
invalid.why: Path-traversal safety on READ, because observed-download manifests are untrusted third-party descriptions.

invalid.name: duplicate-relpath
invalid.why: relpath is an entry's identity; duplicates leave no canonical ordering.

invalid.name: naive-timestamp
invalid.why: A provenance timestamp without an offset is not an instant (docs/decisions.md D-05).

invalid.name: unknown-entry-field
invalid.why: Unknown fields are covered by body_hash, so tolerating them in one implementation and dropping them in another makes one manifest hash two ways (docs/decisions.md D-07).

invalid.name: null-instead-of-absent
invalid.why: The format omits absent fields rather than writing null; accepting both spellings would give one manifest two canonical forms.

invalid.name: float-size
invalid.why: 1.0 and 1 are the same number but different bytes.

invalid.name: digest-wrong-length
invalid.why: A 32-character digest under sha256 means the manifest was assembled from md5s under the wrong header — a mass verification failure waiting to happen.

invalid.name: crc32-without-container
invalid.why: (2.0) A member carrying crc32 but no container to anchor it can never be confirmed (container-model §8).

invalid.name: nested-containers
invalid.why: (2.0) One source_root nested under another is ambiguous for member matching and is forbidden (container-model §8).

invalid.name: orphan-container
invalid.why: (2.0) A declared container with no member under its source_root (spec §8).
